facts.claim: A company must not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business to be eligible for DPIIT startup recognition.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognition
facts.evidence: The entity should not have been formed by splitting up or reconstructing an existing business.

facts.claim: A company must work towards the development or improvement of a product, process, or service and/or have a scalable business model with high potential for wealth and employment generation to be eligible for DPIIT startup recognition.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognition
facts.evidence: The entity should work towards the development or improvement of a product, process, or service and/or have a scalable business model with high potential for wealth and employment generation.

facts.claim: A company must be incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership, or Cooperative Society to be eligible for DPIIT startup recognition.

facts.evidence: Incorporated as a Private Limited Company, Registered Partnership Firm, Limited Liability Partnership, or Cooperative Society.

facts.claim: A company must not exceed an annual turnover of Rs. 200 crore in any financial year since incorporation to be eligible for DPIIT startup recognition.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognition
facts.evidence: The annual turnover should not exceed Rs. 200 crore in any financial year since incorporation.

facts.claim: A company must not exceed a period of existence and operations of 10 years from the date of incorporation to be eligible for DPIIT startup recognition.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognition
facts.evidence: The period of existence and operations should not exceed 10 years from the date of incorporation.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups can self-certify compliance with 6 labour laws and 3 environmental laws through a simple online procedure.

facts.evidence: Startups shall be allowed to self-certify compliance with 6 labour laws and 3 environmental laws through a simple online procedure.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups within 10 years of incorporation are eligible for self-certification of compliance.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognition
facts.evidence: DPIIT recognised startups that are within 10 years within date of incorporation ( 20 if deeptech recognized).

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups can get tax exemption under Section 80IAC for 3 consecutive financial years out of their first ten years since incorporation.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognised_startup
facts.evidence: Eligible startups can be exempted from paying income tax for 3 consecutive financial years out of their first ten years since incorporation.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups can register on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) as sellers to sell their products and services directly to Government entities.

facts.evidence: DPIIT Recognized Startups can register on GeM as sellers and sell their products and services directly to Government entities.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups are exempted from submitting Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security while filling government tenders.
facts.subject: dpiit_recognised_startup
facts.evidence: DPIIT recognised startups have been exempted from submitting Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) or bid security while filling government tenders.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups can be wound up within 90 days of filing an application for insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.

facts.evidence: startups with simple debt structures, or those meeting certain income specified criteria* can be wound up within 90 days of filing an application for insolvency.

facts.claim: DPIIT recognised startups can fast-track their patent applications for examination.

facts.evidence: Patent applications filed by startups shall be fast-tracked for examination so that their value can be realised sooner.

facts.evidence: Startups shall be provided an 80% rebate in filing of patents vis-a-vis other companies.
